title: IoT-based Efficient Streetlight Controlling, Monitoring and Real-time Error Detection System for Smart Cities in Bangladesh
data_type: LDR current traffic and controller observations
anomaly_definition: laboratory LDR-cover state/sensor mismatch
key_finding: Multi-sensor state mismatch can be surfaced but the intervention is laboratory-only.
transfer_limit: No cabinet-AMI-only or repair outcome; LDR obstruction and controller/sensor behavior are confounded.
allowed_claim: Context-plus-electrical mismatch is an anomaly sign when context is independently measured.
prohibited_claim: Field lamp/controller fault; AMI-only validation; portable accuracy or threshold.

title: On the Way: Automated fault detection and diagnostics for LED street lighting systems
data_type: input voltage current power and human-observed light behavior
anomaly_definition: controlled long-duration undervoltage service-disruption patterns
key_finding: A common undervoltage condition produced distinct service disruptions and voltage alone did not determine cause.
transfer_limit: Twelve laboratory luminaires under programmable undervoltage differ from Suyeong cabinet AMI.
allowed_claim: Multi-signal and duration evidence can prioritize inspection.
prohibited_claim: Copying thresholds; field fault probability; root-cause diagnosis from one channel.

title: A Low-Cost and Noninvasive System for the Measurement and Detection of Faulty Streetlights
data_type: vehicle light-meter GPS and repeated route observations
anomaly_definition: illumination-map departure before and after government repair
key_finding: Repeated optical observation is an independent outcome modality complementary to electrical screening.
transfer_limit: Optical outcome is not cabinet current and is sensitive to weather adjacent luminaires route/GPS and calibration.
allowed_claim: AMI candidates can be checked with repeated optical or field observation.
prohibited_claim: Current-only event is a confirmed outage; optical screening alone is Gold.

title: Detection of Anomalies in the Operation of a Road Lighting System Based on Data from Smart Electricity Meters
data_type: per-phase voltage current active/apparent power power factor and controller context
anomaly_definition: forecast departure in cabinet-level road-lighting meter records
key_finding: Road-lighting cabinet records can support online screening but aggregate measurements do not identify a lamp or root cause.
transfer_limit: Study topology/context are known but unavailable for unlinked Suyeong AMI; labels are not repair outcomes.
allowed_claim: Cabinet-level expected-versus-observed behavior is an inspection candidate with verified context/mapping.
prohibited_claim: Individual asset attribution; fault rate; imported performance or threshold.

title: Anomaly detection in urban lighting systems using autoencoder and transformer algorithms
data_type: per-phase active power downsampled to 15-minute windows
anomaly_definition: day-level period labeled anomalous when an abnormal phenomenon occurred
key_finding: A real lighting platform can run rolling power screening but label root cause and repair protocol are not recoverable.
transfer_limit: Thirty-five anomalous sequences and study-selected thresholds; cause maintenance outcome topology and population transfer unresolved.
allowed_claim: Frozen-baseline power departures can be anomaly signs with abstention and contamination control.
prohibited_claim: Importing F1 sensitivity precision or selected thresholds; field-confirmed fault.

title: Automation System Design for Fault Detection in Street Lighting
data_type: transformer-center line currents known lamp-column counts and equivalent resistance
anomaly_definition: estimated faulty group/location from a line-current model
key_finding: Line current can narrow a group only when membership and component assumptions are authoritative.
transfer_limit: No recoverable blinded field-outcome trial; proposed certainty depends on topology/resistance unavailable for unlinked AMI.
allowed_claim: Authoritative cabinet-line-asset mapping is required for group-level prioritization.
prohibited_claim: Individual lamp diagnosis from an unlinked meter; claimed certainty or field accuracy.

title: An Energy-Fraud Detection-System Capable of Distinguishing Frauds from Other Energy Flow Anomalies in an Urban Environment
data_type: smart-meter load profiles engineered features and locally tagged records
anomaly_definition: fraud versus alternative energy-flow anomalies
key_finding: Alternative-root separation and field-tested suspects show why load departure needs an external outcome and competing-cause workflow.
transfer_limit: Fraud mechanism selected data synthetic augmentation class balance inspections and population differ from streetlighting.
allowed_claim: Retain alternative causes and require independent outcomes before causal claims.
prohibited_claim: Transfer fraud labels classifier accuracy/F1 augmentation thresholds or yield to lighting faults.

title: Detection of Non-Technical Losses Using Smart Meter Data and Supervised Learning
data_type: energy alarms electrical magnitudes and metadata joined to inspections
anomaly_definition: supervised non-technical-loss classification from inspection outcomes
key_finding: External inspection outcomes are the evidence type required to evaluate a meter-based operational model.
transfer_limit: Theft labels and inspection-selection process do not identify streetlight service faults.
allowed_claim: Timestamped inspection/work-order outcomes are required before Gold/Silver or accuracy claims.
prohibited_claim: Transfer theft performance thresholds prevalence or feature importance to lighting.

title: Electricity Theft Detection in AMI Using Customers' Consumption Patterns
data_type: customer consumption patterns and distribution-transformer measurements
anomaly_definition: departure from predictable normal consumption used to shortlist theft areas
key_finding: Meter-relative reference can narrow screening without identifying physical cause.
transfer_limit: Consumer behavior and transformer aggregation differ from scheduled streetlighting.
allowed_claim: Meter identity and stable historical context are prerequisites for a proxy load-departure sign.
prohibited_claim: High/low lighting load is a failed lamp or validated fault class.

title: Entropy-based electricity theft detection in AMI network
data_type: historical consumption-step entropy and thresholding
anomaly_definition: large relative-entropy departure treated as suspicious consumption
key_finding: Historical thresholding requires seasonal and operational alternatives.
transfer_limit: Theft target and consumer behavior differ; entropy has no streetlight root cause.
allowed_claim: Persistent statistical departure is a non-causal feature when alternatives are retained.
prohibited_claim: Entropy or persistence confirms a lamp fault or supplies portable FPR.

title: Detection of non-technical losses in smart meter data based on load curve profiling and time series analysis
data_type: real utility load curves with emulated non-technical-loss events
anomaly_definition: shape/time-series departure from expected profile
key_finding: Load-profile shape and timing define a candidate while causes remain non-unique.
transfer_limit: Emulated events and non-technical-loss target do not validate lighting faults or local thresholds.
allowed_claim: Time-aware profile departure can be a proxy anomaly sign.
prohibited_claim: Emulated-event metrics are field-fault metrics or validate Suyeong AMI.

title: Automated load pattern learning and anomaly detection for enhancing energy management in smart buildings
data_type: time-windowed building load patterns and auxiliary HVAC interpretation
anomaly_definition: departure from learned temporal load patterns
key_finding: Time-window-specific patterns and contextual diagnosis are preferable to one global threshold.
transfer_limit: Building occupancy/HVAC differs and additional data are needed for diagnosis.
allowed_claim: Separate time windows and seek independent contextual data before routing an anomaly.
prohibited_claim: Building anomaly labels learned thresholds or diagnosis prove a lamp fault.

title: A Cluster-Based Method for Calculating Baselines for Residential Loads
data_type: utility load histories and comparable normal-day cohorts
anomaly_definition: counterfactual baseline residual rather than fault detection
key_finding: Baseline is a counterfactual estimate requiring comparable history rather than a label or global default.
transfer_limit: Residential cohort construction differs and residual has no fault root cause.
allowed_claim: Use causal meter-relative baseline with coverage and seasonal comparability checks.
prohibited_claim: Baseline residual is fault truth or permits future-data leakage.

title: CUSUM Control Charts
data_type: ordered measurements with an in-control mean and variability
anomaly_definition: cumulative deviation from an in-control process
key_finding: CUSUM detects sustained mean shifts only after target process shift size and error tradeoff are specified.
transfer_limit: Lighting AMI may violate stability/unchanged-process assumptions; CUSUM is not a diagnostic label.
allowed_claim: A frozen meter-relative cumulative-deviation rule can express persistence evidence.
prohibited_claim: CUSUM alarm is a fault or a substitute for Gold/Silver labels.

title: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook: Measurement Process Characterization
data_type: reference checks calibration repeatability reproducibility stability and uncertainty
anomaly_definition: measurement-process departure and uncertainty characterization
key_finding: Measurement provenance and uncertainty must be separated from asset interpretation.
transfer_limit: Does not define AMI lighting anomalies or diagnose physical causes.
allowed_claim: Retain channel availability calibration clock alignment and uncertainty as separate evidence.
prohibited_claim: Unexplained current departure is an asset fault without a measurement boundary.

title: Reliable stator fault detection based on the induction motor negative sequence current compensation
data_type: phase electrical quantities and compensated negative-sequence current
anomaly_definition: stator-fault signal after accounting for asymmetry sensor error and voltage unbalance
key_finding: Raw phase asymmetry has multiple contributors and needs compensation before a motor-fault interpretation.
transfer_limit: Motor physics phasors compensation model and fault target differ from aggregate streetlighting AMI.
allowed_claim: Phase asymmetry needs explicit confounder controls and may be an inspection sign.
prohibited_claim: RMS magnitudes are negative-sequence current or diagnose a streetlight fault.

title: Contributions to the online fault diagnosis of interturn short circuit in three-phase induction motor by means of negative sequence components
data_type: synchronized phase voltage/current phasors and Fortescue components
anomaly_definition: interturn-short-circuit indicators under voltage-unbalance/load variation
key_finding: Negative-sequence components are derived quantities not phase-current magnitudes.
transfer_limit: Motor mechanism phase order voltage phasor timing and impedance data are absent from RMS-only cabinet AMI.
allowed_claim: A phasor-capable system may evaluate phase behavior with topology and outcome checks.
prohibited_claim: Negative-sequence terminology or motor thresholds for RMS-only LightGuard data.

title: IEEE Recommended Practice for Monitoring Electric Power Quality
data_type: defined power-quality measurements and interpretation practice
anomaly_definition: measurement and terminology standard
key_finding: Polyphase interpretation depends on measurement definitions provenance and source/load context.
transfer_limit: A standard is not a streetlight field trial and creates no event-level fault label.
allowed_claim: Document phase provenance and use conservative phase-asymmetry terminology.
prohibited_claim: A standard alone validates a cabinet anomaly root cause or negative-sequence claim from RMS.

title: Electrical Current Signature-Based Machine Learning Models for Streetlight Fault Prediction in Smart City Infrastructure
data_type: simulated/constructed current-signature features
anomaly_definition: model-class fault prediction using synthetic feature construction
key_finding: Synthetic current-signature results are a design limitation not field support for cabinet AMI classification.
transfer_limit: Synthetic features and absent high-resolution field current prevent validation calibration or transfer.
allowed_claim: Simulation must remain separate from operational validation.
prohibited_claim: Synthetic classifier metrics are LightGuard field evidence or fault probability.

title: TimeSeriesBench: An Industrial-Grade Benchmark for Time Series Anomaly Detection Models
data_type: real synthetic and expert-annotated service time series
anomaly_definition: benchmark anomaly events and latency-aware evaluation
key_finding: Evaluation setting unseen-curve handling event metrics and point adjustment affect reported performance.
transfer_limit: Service metrics are not streetlighting maintenance outcomes.
allowed_claim: Future labeled evaluation should be time-forward meter-disjoint and event/latency-aware.
prohibited_claim: Benchmark concepts validate a LightGuard fault detector or present precision/recall.

title: Current Time Series Anomaly Detection Benchmarks are Flawed and are Creating the Illusion of Progress
data_type: public anomaly benchmarks and label/evaluation audit
anomaly_definition: benchmark flaws including misleading evaluation structure
key_finding: Label construction point adjustment triviality and split design can make anomaly scores non-operational.
transfer_limit: Benchmark audit supplies no road-lighting mechanism or operational label.
allowed_claim: Seal origins/splits before scoring and preserve label provenance.
prohibited_claim: Detector-derived labels injected signals or leaky metrics validate field faults.
